summary:
How much carries over: the layered core runs on all five surfaces with no code change. That core is the layer helper and its fixed interface, the four paint layers (COLOUR AND FADE, DAMAGE, MOSS, OUTLINE AND SHADOW), COMBINE, the bake harness and the same-kind score. What changes per surface is the LAYOUT plus one or two small new layers. Brick needs settings only plus one new GRIME layer (soot over bricks and mortar, mottled mortar). Wood needs the slate LAYOUT with board settings, a 10-node 'turn' so the layers' up-down runs along the grain, and a new CRACKS layer, because DAMAGE's cracks only start at a piece edge. Metal needs a new bars-and-panels layout and a new RIVETS layer; MOSS is reused as rust and DAMAGE as chipped paint. Mud has no pieces, so the pieces become the earth clods (a new seamless cell layout); it needs new RUTS and STONES layers (STONES borrows lib/contrib/stone_tools unchanged). Using MOSS as puddle water is unsure. Mud is the most new code with the weakest score evidence. Gravel needs a stone layout: a copy of stone_tools.polygon_stones that also returns each stone's coordinates and size. It also uses GRIME for the soil and its shadow next to stones.

Counted over 52 tool rows (as is + settings only): brick 34, wood 34, metal 33, mud 33, gravel 33. The rest is mostly small copy-and-change-one-line work (recipe wiring, tests). The 'not useful' rows are the painter generators, tracing tools and Geometry Nodes helpers; the painter generators are the baselines.

Checks run today, all in reuse_trials/inventory_checks/:
(1) All six frozen layer boxes build from the snapshot.
(2) Turning the bundle a quarter makes the shared paint run along wood grain (look check sheet, by eye).
(3) Three settings remove the 'slate tongues' on brick: fade_direction 0, fade_length = streak_width, mottle_tallness 1. This corrects the 05 Lessons claim that brick needs a new paint layer.
(4) Settings above a control's listed range are kept, not cut.
(5) The five baseline first new tiles re-score exactly as stored: brick 0.725, wood 0.619, metal 0.578, mud 0.407, gravel 0.372; colour groups 0.750, 0.622, 0.540, 0.313, 0.242.
(6) A text search shows no shared layer reads 'row', and MOSS and DAMAGE are confined to pieces.

Trap found: importing the snapshot writes a __pycache__ folder into it unless sys.dont_write_bytecode = True. It happened once; I deleted the folder I made, and the checksums still match.

No trial was baked or scored. Verdicts marked 'not tried' are from reading. The look checks are 512-dot colour views and were not scored.

surfaces.plan: No pieces in the picture. One piece per tile would restart its coordinates at the tile edge (a seam) and give one random number for everything, so the pieces are the clods. New CELL LAYOUT (~150-250 nodes): a jittered grid of points with wrapped indices; each dot takes its nearest point (3x3 search); cells stretched along the main rut direction; no gaps. Try two cell sizes (clod ~0.006 tile units, or ground patch ~0.04 with specks making the clods) and keep the better by eye. edge_distance = distance to the nearest cell border; base_height = gentle seamless relief with low basins for water. Shared layers: COLOUR AND FADE as earth (one tone per clod, specks, dry/wet areas); MOSS as water with its clump noise and edge rules off and the big patch gate and damp spots on, lichen as small stones; DAMAGE dark clod rims (unsure); OUTLINE off. New layers truly needed: RUTS (seamless wobbling bands in 2-3 directions with dark band, lit bank, groove, wet streaks, sunk height; hp_tools warp) and STONES (polygon_stones unchanged). PUDDLES only if MOSS-as-water shows the clod mosaic. Stack: colour_and_fade, ruts, moss, stones, damage. Measure once: palette_k16.json, non-earth share 31%, fitted_distributions_mud.json and sampler_stats_mud.json summaries; never ruts_main_mud.json or element files. Score against all other references as a control; judge by eye.

surfaces.plan: New STONE LAYOUT: a copy of lib/contrib/stone_tools.polygon_stones in reuse_trials/gravel/ that also returns each stone's centre offset and radius. Two or three grid sizes (e.g. 12, 30, 70 cells); the biggest stone wins. piece = stone; local_x/local_y = offset/(2 radius)+0.5; piece_width/height = 2 radius in tile units; edge_distance = minus the inside distance; gap = soil; base_height = stone dome, soil low next to a stone rising over ~8 dots (only within the stone's own cell). Shared layers by settings: COLOUR AND FADE stone palette with a large tone spread, blue-grey and brownish tints, fade_direction -1; DAMAGE pale flakes and pits as rust; OUTLINE gap colour = soil base, thin rim, no shadow or lip; MOSS off or a few rust spots. New: GRIME (shared with brick) for the soil mottle and the low-spot shadow; FACETS only if the stones look flat (same idea as RIVETS' slices). Measure once: scores/measurements.json, window_spread.json, description/S_v4.json class counts and radii; never stones_found.json. Risks: a grid look (the warp helps), stones limited to about half a cell, and the shadow only reaches the own cell's stone. Then a 1254 full bake, three seed sets, tests.
